===============================================================================
RESIDENTIAL DWELLING INSURANCE
GENERAL POLICY CONDITIONS - PROPERTY DAMAGE COVER
===============================================================================

These conditions apply together with the General Contract Provisions and with
the Schedule, both of which form part of this contract. Sums insured, limits,
deductibles, periods and percentages shown in square brackets are those stated
in the Schedule.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - PURPOSE AND KEY CONCEPTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 What this insurance does

Combined residential buildings insurance protects the policyholder against the
financial consequences of physical damage to their building. The perils that can
be insured are the ones bundled together in these conditions - fire, escape of
water, storm and hail, and further natural hazards among them. Which of the
insurable perils are actually covered is agreed between insurer and policyholder
and recorded in the schedule.

Where insured property is destroyed or damaged, the insurer indemnifies the cost
of putting it back in the same kind and quality. Alongside the building itself,
the cover extends to the ancillary structures standing on the insured site
insofar as they are insured property under Part 4. A range of consequential
expenses triggered by a loss event - clearance and disposal of the material
arising among them - is also carried.

1.2 How the wording is to be read

Personal designations are to be understood as gender-neutral throughout; no
parallel male and female forms are used.

1.3 Explanation of recurring terms (not legally binding)

Policyholder - the insurer's contracting party and the purchaser of the cover.

Insured event - the event for which the insurer pays.

Affected part - a room, a surface, a structure, a building component or an item
in which physical damage caused by the insured event has been established by the
loss investigation. The affected parts, taken together, delimit what the insurer
indemnifies.

Repair cost - outlay that serves to put an affected part back into the condition
it was in immediately before the insured event. Outlay that serves another
purpose - preservation, upkeep, protection against future influences, the
improvement of the ground, or the running of a contractor's business - is not a
repair cost, whatever heading it is invoiced under.

Material arising - the broken, displaced or otherwise unusable material that an
insured event leaves on the insured site, together with the material that the
clearance work generates. It falls into distinct categories according to how it
must be routed for disposal: vegetal material, timber, mineral and aggregate
material, glazed material, and soil.

Itemised charge - a position that states the labour actually worked, or the
material actually supplied, together with its quantity and its rate. A position
that states neither, and instead prices an operation as a whole, is not an
itemised charge.

Exclusion - a peril, a type of damage, an item of property or a type of outlay
for which no cover exists.

Duties - the things the policyholder must do or refrain from doing before, during
and after an insured event.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - INSURED PERILS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 The perils that can be covered

The insurer indemnifies insured property that is destroyed or damaged by, or lost
as a consequence of, the following events:

  (a) FIRE GROUP - fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning;
      explosion; deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft, its
      parts or its cargo; impact of a vehicle; scorching; smoke and soot.

  (b) ESCAPE OF WATER.

  (c) NATURAL HAZARDS, in two tiers:
        (c1) storm and hail;
        (c2) the further natural hazards - flood, backing-up of water,
             earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and
             volcanic eruption.

2.2 How the groups combine

Each of the three groups (a), (b) and (c1) can be taken separately. The further
natural hazards under (c2) can only be taken in combination with one or more of
the perils in (a), (b) or (c1); they are not available on a standalone basis.

2.5 Natural hazards defined

2.5.1 Storm
Storm means a weather-driven movement of air reaching at least the gale threshold
on the recognised scale of wind strength, expressed as a defined minimum
sustained wind speed.

Where the wind strength at the loss location cannot be established, storm is
presumed if the policyholder demonstrates either of the following:
  (a) in the vicinity of the insured site the air movement caused damage to
      buildings that were in sound condition, or to other property of comparable
      resistance; or
  (b) given the sound condition of the insured property, the damage can only have
      arisen through storm.

2.5.2 Hail
Hail means solid precipitation in the form of grains of ice.

2.5.3 Which storm and hail events are covered
Only damage arising in one of the following ways is covered:
  (a) storm or hail acts directly on insured property, or on structures in which
      insured property is located; consequential damage to insured property
      arising from this is covered;
  (b) storm or hail acts directly on structures joined to the insured building or
      to an insured site installation;
  (c) storm or hail throws building parts, trees, branches, masonry or other
      objects onto insured property, or onto structures in which insured property
      is located; consequential damage to insured property arising from this is
      covered.

2.5.4 The further natural hazards
The further natural hazards are flood, backing-up of water, earthquake, ground
subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and volcanic eruption, each as
customarily defined in these conditions.

2.5.5 Effect on ancillary structures
Ancillary structures standing on the insured site - and their cladding, glazing,
roofing, fastenings and applied finishes - are within the cover on the same terms
as the building itself, insofar as they are insured property under Part 4.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - EXCLUSIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 General exclusions

3.1.1 War
Damage caused by war, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or
insurrection is not covered. This applies irrespective of any contributing
causes.

3.1.2 Civil commotion
Damage caused by internal civil unrest is not covered. This applies irrespective
of any contributing causes.

3.1.3 Nuclear energy
Damage caused by nuclear energy, nuclear radiation or radioactive substances is
not covered. This applies irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.4 Exclusions within the natural hazards

Damage caused by the following is not covered, irrespective of any contributing
causes except where such causes are named below:
  (a) storm surge;
  (b) the penetration of rain, hail, snow or dirt through windows, doors or other
      openings that were not properly closed. This exclusion does not apply where
      those openings were created by storm or hail and constitute damage to the
      insured property;
  (c) groundwater, except insofar as it emerged at the surface as a result of
      precipitation or of the overflow of surface waters;
  (d) the perils of the fire group, unless triggered by an insured natural
      hazard;
  (e) drought or desiccation;
  (f) the ordinary weathering, fading, decay, insect attack or gradual
      deterioration of exposed surfaces, finishes and timber, and the
      consequences of an omitted or overdue protective treatment.

Damage to structures that are not ready for use, and to property located within
them, is not covered.

3.5 Work beyond the affected parts, and outlay that is not a repair cost

Work carried out beyond those parts of the insured property that were themselves
affected by the insured event is not covered. Work carried out on, in or to
property that is not insured property is not covered, save for the clearance
expressly provided for in 5.2.1. Outlay that does not constitute a repair cost is
not indemnified. The delimitation in each case is governed by 7.1.5 to 7.1.9.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - INSURED PROPERTY, INSURED LOCATION, DEDUCTIBLES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 What is insured

Insured property comprises:
  (a) the buildings identified in the schedule;
  (b) their building components;
  (c) their building accessories;
  (d) terraces on the insured site that directly adjoin the building;
  (e) further site installations.

4.2 The categories defined

4.2.1 Building and dwelling
Buildings are structures connected to the ground. They must be capable of
affording protection against external influences and, for the purposes of these
conditions, must be intended for predominantly residential use.

4.2.2 Building components
Building components are items incorporated into a building or into an insured
site installation that have lost their independence through their firm connection
with it. Glazing elements, panes, cladding boards, roofing elements, doors,
hatches, fastenings and the applied surface finishes count as building components
of the structure to which they belong.

4.2.4 Terraces
Terraces are paved surfaces intended for occupation in the open air that directly
adjoin the building, together with their bedding, jointing and edge restraint.

4.2.5 Further site installations
Further site installations means, exclusively, the ancillary structures of light
construction standing on the insured site and serving the storage, upkeep or
amenity of the insured building, together with the components listed in 4.2.2
belonging to them.

4.3 Property not insured

Not insured:
  (a) photovoltaic installations and their components;
  (b) all items subsequently incorporated into the building or into a site
      installation by a tenant or by a condominium owner where that person both
      procured or took the items over at their own expense and bears the risk for
      them;
  (c) electronically stored data and programs;
  (d) the ground and soil of the insured site; paths, drives, standings and other
      laid or paved surfaces that are not terraces within the meaning of 4.2.4;
      and the bedding, jointing, grit, chippings and other aggregate material
      belonging to such surfaces. Work of every kind on such property - taking
      up, replacing, re-laying, levelling, regrading or disposing of it - is not
      indemnified;
  (e) trees, shrubs, hedges, lawns, planted beds and other vegetation, whether
      standing, felled, uprooted or displaced, together with their root bodies.
      Replacement, replanting and re-landscaping are not indemnified. The
      clearance provided for in 5.2.1 is unaffected by this.

4.5 The insured location

The insured location is the insured site: the land parcel or parcels on which the
insured building stands, together with the structures standing on it.

4.7 Deductibles

A deductible is the share of the indemnity, or the amount, that the policyholder
bears itself per insured event. The deductible stated in the schedule is deducted
once from the indemnity for the insured event, irrespective of how many trades,
invoices or heads of claim are involved.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - INSURED COSTS, LOSS OF RENT AND RENTAL VALUE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Which costs are covered

The insurer reimburses the following costs where they were necessary as a
consequence of an insured event and were actually incurred:
  (a) clearance, debris removal, demolition and disposal costs;
  (b) costs of moving and protecting property;
  (c) costs of emergency and loss-mitigation measures;
  (d) hotel costs;
  (e) costs of returning early from a holiday.

Reimbursement of each of these heads is limited to the amount agreed for it.

5.2 The cost heads defined

5.2.1 Clearance, debris removal and disposal
Costs incurred in clearing away and demolishing insured property, and in clearing
the insured site of the material arising. This includes gathering and loading
that material, sorting or sieving it where the disposal route requires it,
transporting it to the nearest suitable disposal site, depositing it and
destroying it.

The clearance extends to material that is not itself insured property, insofar as
the insured event deposited, displaced, broke up or churned it up and it has to
be taken away in order to make the insured site usable again. To that extent the
exclusions in 4.3(d) and 4.3(e) do not apply.

Disposal of any one category of the material arising is indemnified once per
insured event. Where more than one charge is raised for the disposal of the same
category - on the same invoice, on a second invoice of the same contractor, or on
the invoice of another trade instructed on the same loss - only the first such
charge is indemnified, whatever wording, sub-description or degree of processing
the further charges carry. The categories are those named in 1.3, and a further
charge remains a charge in the same category even where it describes a different
form, part or fraction of the same kind of material.

Not indemnified under this head are:
  (a) excavating, digging out, levelling, regrading or replacing the ground and
      soil beyond what the clearance of displaced material requires;
  (b) taking up, removing or disposing of the material of surfaces falling under
      4.3(d), and of the aggregate and bedding material belonging to them,
      irrespective of whether the insured event displaced it;
  (c) grubbing out, cutting out or removing the root bodies and standing remains
      of the vegetation falling under 4.3(e), as distinct from clearing away the
      material lying on the site.

5.2.2 Moving and protecting property
Costs incurred in moving, altering or protecting other property, reimbursable
where those measures serve to reinstate or replace insured property.

5.2.3 Emergency and loss-mitigation measures
Costs of the measures reasonably taken immediately after an insured event to make
the insured property and the insured site safe and to prevent further damage,
including the labour required for them.

5.2.4 Hotel costs
Costs of accommodation in a hotel or similar, excluding incidentals such as
breakfast. The precondition is that the dwelling permanently occupied by the
policyholder has become uninhabitable and that confining themselves to a
habitable part of it cannot reasonably be expected of them. The loss of use of an
ancillary structure, of a garden or of another part of the insured site that is
not itself living accommodation does not render a dwelling uninhabitable within
the meaning of this head.

5.3 Loss of rent and rental value

The insurer reimburses loss of rent where tenants of residential premises have
lawfully stopped paying rent in whole or in part on account of an insured event,
and the locally customary rental value of residential premises occupied by the
policyholder itself where, on account of the insured event, the policyholder
cannot reasonably be expected to use at least parts of the dwelling.

5.4 The period for loss of rent and rental value

Loss of rent or rental value is reimbursed for the period during which the rooms
are unusable, but for no longer than [number] months from the occurrence of the
insured event, and only to the extent that the policyholder has not culpably
delayed the resumption of use.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 6 - BASIS OF COVER AND PREMIUM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 Insurable value

The insurable value forms the basis for calculating the indemnity. The insurable
value determined for the building applies equally to building accessories,
terraces and further site installations as defined in 4.2.

6.2 Index-linked reinstatement value with enhancement

What is insured is the locally customary new-build value of the insured property
identified in the schedule, taken at the time of the insured event, together with
the additional costs arising from public-law restrictions on reinstatement and
the price increases arising between the occurrence of the insured event and
reinstatement initiated without delay.

6.3 Index-linked current value with enhancement where reinstatement is omitted or
    delayed

For property that is not reinstated, or is reinstated late, only the index-linked
current value with enhancement is insured - the enhanced new-build value at the
time of the insured event, less depreciation for age and for the degree of wear.

6.5 How the premium is calculated

The bases for calculating the premium are the area, the building type, the
construction and the fit-out, the use, other agreed features material to the
premium calculation, and the adjustment factor.

6.6 Adjustment of cover and premium

Where cover is adjusted in line with the development of building costs, the
premium changes accordingly, by way of the adjustment factor taking effect from
1 January of each year.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 7 - CALCULATION AND PAYMENT OF THE INDEMNITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 Basis of calculation

7.1.1 The insurer reimburses:
  (a) for destroyed buildings and destroyed site installations - the locally
      customary reinstatement costs, taken at the time of the insured event;
  (b) for damaged buildings, damaged site installations and other damaged
      property - the necessary repair costs at the time of the insured event,
      capped at the insurable value at that time;
  (c) for destroyed or lost other property - the replacement price for property
      of the same kind and quality in new condition, taken at the time of the
      insured event.

7.1.4 The achievable sale price of remains is set off in calculating the
indemnity. Where the material arising has no realisable value, no set-off arises
and its disposal is governed by 5.2.1.

7.1.5 Extent of the repair
Indemnity is confined to those parts of the insured property that were themselves
affected by the insured event. The affected parts are the rooms, surfaces,
structures, building components and items in which physical damage caused by the
event is established by the loss investigation - by inspection, by photographic
record, or by technical measurement taken at or shortly after the time of the
loss.

Work carried out on a structure, a surface, a component or an item that was not
itself affected is not covered. This applies even where the work is carried out
  (a) so that treated and untreated parts correspond in appearance, colour,
      pattern, format or material;
  (b) for reasons of convenience, or because treating a whole structure or surface
      is more economical than treating the affected part of it;
  (c) at the same time as covered work, in the course of it, or as part of the
      same overall project; or
  (d) by the same contractor as the covered work, and invoiced together with it.

7.1.6 Continuous surfaces
Where only part of a single continuous surface was affected, indemnity extends to
the treatment of the adjoining unaffected sections of that same surface only where
a replacement material corresponding to the original is no longer obtainable and a
visible discontinuity would otherwise remain. It does not extend to a separate
structure, nor to a surface, component or item that does not form part of the same
continuous affected surface.

7.1.7 Preparatory and ancillary work
The necessary repair costs under 7.1.1(b) include:
  (a) taking down, dismantling and disposing of the affected components,
      claddings, glazing elements and finishes;
  (b) the cleaning, stripping back and preparation of the substrate necessary
      before a new finish is applied or a new element fitted;
  (c) materials of a type, quality, grade and specification corresponding to those
      in place immediately before the insured event, including replacement glazing
      elements and panes, boards, fixings, and the ordinary finishing products
      applied to the repaired part;
  (d) the labour of the workers of each trade necessarily deployed on the covered
      work, at the ordinary rate of that trade for the category of worker actually
      deployed. Labour is indemnified whether it is billed as one position or as
      several positions covering distinct operations, provided each position is an
      itemised charge within the meaning of 1.3 and corresponds to work actually
      carried out on the affected parts or on the clearance under 5.2.1;
  (e) one travel, vehicle or call-out charge per trade invoice.

The rate charged for labour under (d) is taken to cover the deployment of the
worker together with everything the worker needs in order to work; see 7.1.8(b).

7.1.8 Outlay that is not a repair cost
The following do not constitute repair costs and are not indemnified, however they
may be described or invoiced:

  (a) measures directed at the general condition, cleanliness, tidiness, upkeep,
      preservation, modernisation or improvement of the insured property, as
      distinct from making good the damage caused by the insured event. Treatments
      and products whose purpose or effect is to protect a surface against future
      weathering, ultraviolet light, moisture, decay or infestation belong to this
      heading and are not indemnified, irrespective of whether they are applied in
      the course of covered work, on an affected part, or by the same contractor
      as the covered work. This does not affect the ordinary finishing products
      under 7.1.7(c), nor the clearance and disposal under 5.2.1;

  (b) outlay belonging to a contractor's own business operation rather than to the
      repair. This heading covers, in particular, the contractor's own tools,
      kits, sets, brushes, blades, ladders and consumable small equipment; its own
      diagnostic and measuring devices; the machines, powered plant, appliances
      and equipment it deploys in order to carry out the work, whether charged at
      time, by unit, as a deployment or utilisation charge, or otherwise; the
      catering, refreshment and provisioning of its own personnel; and general
      administrative, handling, processing or coordination charges levied in
      addition to itemised labour and materials. Outlay of this kind is deemed to
      be included in the labour rate under 7.1.7(d) and is not separately
      indemnified;

  (c) the same item of cost where it is invoiced more than once in respect of the
      same insured event, whether by one contractor or across several trades; only
      the first such charge is indemnified. Two charges are the same item of cost
      where they relate to the same operation, the same part or the same category
      of material, even where they appear on different invoices, under different
      trade headings, or in different words. In particular, where a trade bills the
      labour and the materials of an operation as itemised charges and, in
      addition, a position pricing that same operation as a whole, the itemised
      charges are indemnified and the additional position is not;

  (d) more than one travel, vehicle, call-out, return-visit or re-attendance charge
      on the same invoice.

7.1.9 No improvement on the pre-loss standard
Reinstatement proceeds on the basis of the type, quality, grade and specification
in place immediately before the insured event. Where a higher specification, a
larger format, a superior material, a longer-lasting or more resistant product or
a premium range is chosen instead, indemnity is limited to the cost of an
equivalent standard-grade replacement corresponding to what was in place before
the loss; the difference is borne by the policyholder. Products falling under
7.1.8(a) are not indemnified at all and are not brought back into cover by this
provision.

7.4 Costs

Insured costs under Part 5 are reimbursed where it is demonstrated that they were
actually incurred. The indemnity limits agreed for each head are applied.

7.7 Value added tax

Value added tax is reimbursed only if and to the extent that it was actually
incurred on the occasion of the reinstatement or replacement. It is not reimbursed
where the policyholder is entitled to recover input tax.

7.8 Deductible

Deductibles are deducted from the indemnity in the amount agreed.

7.9 When the indemnity falls due

The indemnity falls due once the insurer has conclusively determined the claim as
to its basis and its amount. One month after notifying the loss, the policyholder
may claim as an interim payment the amount that is, on the prevailing assessment,
payable as a minimum.

7.13 Deferral of payment

The insurer may defer payment for as long as there is doubt as to the
policyholder's entitlement to receive payment, official or criminal proceedings
arising out of this insured event are still pending, or a legally required
involvement of a secured lender has not taken place.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 8 - EXPERT DETERMINATION PROCEDURE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 Determining the amount of the loss
After an insured event has occurred, the policyholder may require that the amount
of the loss be determined in an expert determination procedure. Insurer and
policyholder may also agree on such a procedure jointly.

8.3 Procedure before the determination
Each party is to nominate one expert in text form - by email, fax or letter, for
example. Before beginning their determinations, the two experts nominate in text
form a third expert as umpire. Where the experts cannot agree on the umpire, it is
appointed by the court with local jurisdiction for the loss location, on the
application of either party.

8.4 Content of the determination
The experts' findings must state a schedule of the destroyed and the damaged
insured property together with the corresponding insurable values at the time of
the insured event, the reinstatement and replacement costs, the residual values,
and the insured costs and the insured loss of rent or rental value.

8.5 Procedure after the determination
Each expert transmits its findings to both parties simultaneously. Where the two
sets of findings diverge, the umpire decides the points that remain in dispute,
within the limits set by the experts' findings. The findings of the experts, or of
the umpire, are binding on the contracting parties. They are not binding where it
is demonstrated that they manifestly deviate substantially from the true state of
affairs.

8.6 Costs
Unless something else has been agreed, each party bears the costs of its own
expert. The costs of the umpire are borne by the two parties in equal shares.

8.7 Duties remain unaffected
The expert determination procedure does not affect the policyholder's duties.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 9 - POLICYHOLDER DUTIES AND INCREASE IN RISK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.1 Contractually agreed safety requirements before an insured event

9.1.1 Insured property must be kept in proper condition at all times. This applies
in particular to roofs and roof coverings, to items attached to the exterior, to
the fastenings of ancillary structures, and to exposed timber and surface
finishes, which must be maintained and re-treated at the intervals ordinarily
required for them. Defects or damage must be remedied without delay.

9.1.2 Structures or parts of structures that are not in use must be inspected
sufficiently frequently at every time of year.

9.1.4 To avoid flood and backing-up damage, backflow prevention devices must be
kept operational and the drainage lines on the insured site kept clear.

9.2 Duties after an insured event

The policyholder must avert and mitigate the loss so far as it reasonably can,
must make the insured property and the insured site safe without delay, and must
preserve the affected parts and the material arising for inspection until the
insurer has had the opportunity to establish the extent of the damage.

9.3 Consequences of a breach of duty

Where the policyholder breaches one of the duties in 9.1 or 9.2, the following
applies, subject to the conditions set out in the general contract provisions: the
insurer is entitled to terminate the contract. It may also be wholly or partly
released from liability.

9.4 Circumstances constituting an increase in risk

An increase in risk subject to notification under the general contract provisions
may exist in particular where a circumstance changes about which the insurer asked
before the contract was concluded; where the building or the predominant part of
it is no longer in use; where construction work renders it predominantly unusable;
or where a commercial operation is taken up or changed on the insured site.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 10 - CANCELLATION, SECURED LENDERS, TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

10.1 Cancellation where a security right has been registered

Where a secured lender has registered its charge over the property, cancellation
of the insurance relationship by the policyholder in respect of the fire peril
group is effective only where the policyholder demonstrated, at least one month
before expiry of the insurance contract, that the property was no longer
encumbered with the charge, or that the secured lender consented to the
cancellation. This does not apply to a cancellation following a disposal of the
property, or to a cancellation in the insured event.

10.2 Legal position following a transfer of ownership

Where the policyholder disposes of the insured property, the acquirer steps into
its place in the insurance contract at the date of registration in the land
register, and from that time takes over the rights and obligations of the
policyholder. Seller and acquirer are jointly and severally liable for the premium
for the insurance period in which the transfer of ownership occurs. The insurer
need only recognise the acquirer's entry once it becomes aware of it.

10.3 Rights of cancellation on a transfer of ownership

The insurer is entitled to cancel the contract as against the acquirer on one
month's notice, that right lapsing if it is not exercised within one month of the
insurer becoming aware of the disposal. The acquirer is entitled to cancel with
immediate effect or with effect from the end of the current insurance period, in
text form, that right lapsing one month after the acquisition. In either case the
seller alone remains liable for payment of the premium.

10.4 Duties of notification

The disposal must be notified to the insurer without delay, in text form, by the
seller or by the acquirer. Where that notification has been omitted, the insurer
is not obliged to pay in the insured event on the conditions set out in the
general contract provisions.

===============================================================================
END OF DOCUMENT
===============================================================================
case.description:
During a storm, a large tree came down onto the garden shed. The roof took the brunt of it, and the impact was enough that the whole structure needed proper attention afterward, not just a quick patch — a couple of skilled workers spent the better part of two days on the shed itself, and it ended up getting fully repainted and resealed against the weather (fresh coat, protective UV treatment, all the trim redone), rather than just having the damaged section fixed.

Dealing with the tree took a separate crew with a saw and some heavier machinery to get it cut up and cleared off the roof. Underneath and around it, the ground had been churned up — roots, excavated soil, and displaced paving material all needed sorting out. Between the tree removal and the ground work, there was a fair amount of material to haul away: old wood from the damaged roof, green waste from the tree, the excavated soil, broken paving, and a glass pane from the shed that had been broken too. A separate waste and recycling service handled the disposal side of things.
